extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewers evaluating NeurIPS 2022 submissions, covering conduct, procedural duties, review form fields, scoring rubrics, and best practices for writing and discussing reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and agree to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct while performing reviewer duties (including writing reviews and participating in discussions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must continue to abide by the Code of Conduct throughout reviewing; there is a link to the Code of Conduct on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest declaration and checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must read what constitutes a conflict of interest for NeurIPS 2022 and declare conflicts in their profile; check conflicts as soon as papers are assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assigned a paper that creates a conflict, or you are unqualified to review, notify your Area Chair (AC) immediately. Do not attempt to deduce author identities (deanonymize submissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are expected to bid on papers in the bidding period; bids are important input to the matching process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deceptive bidding to influence outcomes is prohibited and may prompt ethics investigations and removal from future committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and adherence to key dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete review tasks within the specified dates (reviewing, author rebuttal, discussion phases, metareviews, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot complete a review on time, inform your AC as soon as possible. Participate promptly in discussion phases (author-reviewer, reviewer-AC, metareview).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: OpenReview profile & communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure your OpenReview profile is up to date (preferred email) and monitor OpenReview emails (noreply@openreview.net).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whitelist noreply@openreview.net if necessary. Use the reviewer console in OpenReview to see assignments and tasks. Contact the AC by leaving an OpenReview comment with the AC as a reader; contact program chairs only if unresolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary reviewer responsibility: write thoughtful, substantiated reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be informative, substantiated, and useful; superficial or uninformed reviews are worse than none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make reviews useful to authors, other reviewers, and AC/SACs. Provide constructive suggestions, avoid vague statements, and support claims with evidence or clear reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NeurIPS paper checklist as a tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may use the NeurIPS paper checklist included in each paper or supplementary materials to guide evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answering 'no' to some checklist items is typically not grounds for rejection; authors should not be punished for honestly stating limitations. Some submissions may include the checklist in supplementary material by mistake—view at your discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging ethical concerns / ethics review
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper raises ethical issues, flag it for an ethics review so ethics reviewers will be assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics reviewers' comments will be visible to reviewers, the AC, and authors and should be used to inform deliberations. See the NeurIPS ethics guidelines for guidance on when to flag a paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep everything related to the review process confidential; do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions until they are public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share submissions or discuss them with others without program chairs' approval. Submitted code cannot be redistributed or used for other purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The process is double-blind at the reviewer and AC level; reviewers and ACs cannot see author identities and must not attempt to find them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are responsible for anonymizing submissions (including supplementary and linked materials). If a submission is not adequately anonymized, contact the corresponding AC rather than attempting to deanonymize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety when executing submitted code or following links
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat submitted code and linked content as untrusted; exercise caution running code or visiting links provided by authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended safe execution environments: (1) inside a Docker container, (2) a virtual machine (VirtualBox/VMWare), or (3) a network-isolated cloud instance. Be mindful that links may log IP addresses or contain vulnerabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary field guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief summary of the paper and its contributions; this is not the place for critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should generally agree with a well-written summary. Keep it factual and concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths and Weaknesses (overall assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a thorough assessment of the paper's strengths and weaknesses, addressing originality, quality, clarity, and significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Touch on each sub-dimension (originality, quality, clarity, significance). Be specific so authors can act on feedback. Avoid vague statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the tasks or methods are new, or whether the work is a novel combination of known techniques; clarify how it differs from prior contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether related work is adequately cited and whether novelty is substantive rather than incremental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality (technical soundness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the submission is technically sound: are claims well supported through theoretical analysis or experiments and are methods appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the work is complete or work-in-progress, and whether authors honestly evaluate strengths and weaknesses. Flag major technical flaws or unsupported claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the submission is clearly written and well organized, and whether it adequately informs the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong paper should provide enough information for an expert reader to reproduce results. If unclear, provide constructive suggestions for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether results are important and whether others are likely to use or build on the ideas; does the work advance the state of the art or address a difficult task better than previous work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider unique data, unique conclusions, or unique theoretical/experimental approaches when judging significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions (actionable items for authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: List and carefully describe questions and suggestions where an author response could change your opinion, clarify confusion, or address limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on issues that can be resolved in rebuttal or discussion; be specific and constructive to facilitate a productive rebuttal phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations & societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether authors have adequately addressed limitations and potential negative societal impacts of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not adequately discussed, include constructive suggestions. Authors should be rewarded, not punished, for transparently reporting limitations and potential negative impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns field
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit field to indicate ethical concerns; flag for an ethics review when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NeurIPS ethics guidelines for what qualifies; flagging prompts assignment of ethics reviewers whose comments are visible to the PC/reviewers/authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness numeric rating (1-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric rating indicating the soundness of technical claims, methodology, experiments and whether central claims are adequately supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale: 4=excellent, 3=good, 2=fair, 1=poor. Use this to communicate methodological rigor and evidence support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation numeric rating (1-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric rating for quality of presentation, including writing style, clarity, and contextualization relative to prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale: 4=excellent, 3=good, 2=fair, 1=poor. Consider clarity and sufficiency of information for comprehension and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution numeric rating (1-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric rating for the overall contribution quality to the research area: importance of questions, originality, and value of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale: 4=excellent, 3=good, 2=fair, 1=poor. Evaluate how valuable the ideas/results are for the NeurIPS community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (1-10) with descriptive guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall numeric score from 1 (Very Strong Reject) to 10 (Award quality) with associated qualitative descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed descriptors: 10=Award quality, technically flawless with groundbreaking impact; 9=Very Strong Accept; 8=Strong Accept; 7=Accept; 6=Weak Accept; 5=Borderline accept (use sparingly); 4=Borderline reject (use sparingly); 3=Reject (technical flaws, weak evaluation, poor reproducibility); 2=Strong Reject (major technical flaws); 1=Very Strong Reject (trivial results or unaddressed ethical issues). Use examples in descriptors to justify choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report your confidence in your assessment using a 1-5 scale reflecting familiarity with the area and depth of checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5=absolutely certain (very familiar, checked details); 4=confident but not absolute; 3=fairly confident; 2=willing to defend but likely unfamiliar with parts; 1=educated guess (not in your area or difficult to understand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form: support for Markdown/LaTeX
rubrics_metrics.description: The review form allows inclusion of Markdown and LaTeX in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See OpenReview FAQ for formatting questions; use formatting to improve clarity of technical points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices: be thoughtful, fair, useful, specific, flexible, timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Guiding principles for tone and content of reviews: be thoughtful and considerate, fair (avoid personal biases), useful (constructive), specific (actionable), flexible (consider author responses), and timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid crushing first-time authors; update reviews if your opinion changes after rebuttal; notify program chairs if pressured to bias a review; report unethical or suspect behavior to your AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting instructions enforcement guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should follow the NeurIPS submission style and page limits (nine content pages; additional pages allowed for references and the paper checklist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor formatting violations (e.g., a few lines over) are not critical; flag major violations that cannot be rectified without harming presentation to your AC. Additional content beyond allowed pages can be reviewed at your discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS disallows submissions that are identical or substantially similar to papers submitted to or published in other archival venues or to other NeurIPS submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slicing contributions too thinly is discouraged and may violate policy. If you suspect dual submission or need clarification, contact the AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in author-reviewer and reviewer-AC discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: During rebuttal and discussion phases, read all reviews and author responses and engage in open exchange with authors and other reviewers; help ACs during meta-review writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially important for borderline papers and when reviewers disagree. Acknowledge author responses even if they don't change your opinion; revise your review if your evaluation changes and explain why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of reviews (post-decision opt-in)
rubrics_metrics.description: After decisions, a random subset of reviews will be evaluated; reviewers are asked to opt-in to this evaluation to help improve review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is voluntary and will not penalize individual reviewers; results may be used in combination with other signals to reward outstanding reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working relationships with ACs/SACs/Program Chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand roles: ACs are primary contacts, ensure quality reviews, facilitate discussions and write meta-reviews; SACs oversee ACs and help with calibration; program chairs make final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issues cannot be resolved with an AC, contact program chairs at the provided program-chairs@neurips.cc address (do not contact PCs at personal emails).
